result.title: Alert-List Concordance for Evaluating Imputation Strategies in ICU Sepsis Prediction
result.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the 14th Workshop on Data Mining in Biomedical Informatics and Healthcare (DMBIH 2026), held in conjunction with IEEE ICDM 2026
result.summary: Preprocessing is an under-measured reliability risk in clinical prediction: a model can keep a similar AUROC and still change who receives an alert. Imputation quality is commonly evaluated using reconstruction error or aggregate discrimination, neither of which directly measures agreement on which patients are flagged. At a matched alert rate, pipelines with similar aggregate performance can produce different patient lists. This question is especially relevant under the frequent, structured missingness of real ICU records. We therefore introduce alert-list concordance, which asks whether two pipelines identify the same high-risk patients, measured by the Jaccard similarity of their top-k% alert sets with patient-level bootstrap confidence intervals. On PhysioNet/CinC 2019 (40,336 patients, 71.9% missingness), we compare nine imputation strategies and a native-missingness baseline using a fixed XGBoost configuration, fitted and Platt-calibrated separately for each strategy. After Bonferroni correction, 22 of the 28 reconstruction-method pairs showed no statistically significant difference in patient-level AUROC, yet their alert lists overlap at Jaccard 0.518 to 0.750. Similar aggregate discrimination can therefore accompany different patient selections. ForwardFill is a separate outlier, pairing higher discrimination with the lowest overlap in the matrix, 0.40 to 0.45. The broad pattern holds within each hospital system and under six patient-level aggregation rules. At the row level, eight of ten methods fall within an AUROC range of 0.011. In this row-level pipeline, deep imputers did not outperform mean imputation on discrimination, and the sequential implementations cost 5 to 12 times mean imputation in total pipeline wall-clock time on our hardware.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 PhysioNet/CinC 2019 ICU 脓毒症预测上，用固定 XGBoost 配置比较九种插补策略与原生缺失基线，提出 alert-list concordance——以 top-k% 告警集合的 Jaccard 相似度加 bootstrap 置信区间衡量两条流水线是否圈定同一批高风险患者，并给出运行时间成本对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察是「聚合指标相近但选中的样本集合差异很大」，可能为评估不同 LVR 推理路径或视觉证据筛选是否真正定位同一批关键输入、以及如何做稳定性与逐样本一致性评价提供指标设计线索；文中缺失值处理与墙钟时间统计也与推理成本核算有间接联系，具体可迁移性需核查。
